newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to halt direct S.Africa flights in February.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to halt direct S.Africa flights in February.

text.p: Taiwan said on Monday its plan to halt direct flights to South Africa to penalise Pretoria's plan to sever diplomatic ties would take effect on February 15.
Foreign Minister John Chang said Taiwan would give South African Airways a two-month grace period so that it could honour flight reservations already made.
"The purpose (of the delay) is to give South African Airways time to adjust its operations," Chang was quoted by the state-run Central News Agency as saying.
South African has been the only airline offering direct Johannesburg service since Taiwan's China Airlines dropped its money-losing weekly connection a few months ago.

Pretoria, Taiwan's biggest of 30 diplomatic allies, shocked the island in November by announcing it would switch formal ties by the end of 1997 to Beijing, which refuses to recognise states that recognise what it regards as a renegade province.
Taiwan responded by postponing all aid projects and treaties, including flight-rights agreements, and recalling its ambassador.
South African Airways currently flies two weekly round-trip flights between Taipei and Johannesburg.
